issues.description: send_transaction no longer uses CAT wallet but enforces XCH address; previously generated from Wallet (XCH) only by type — behavior consistent, but address validation diverges from prior network-prefix check
issues.detail: Previously send_transaction checked only network prefix against config; now it uses ensure_valid_address with allowed_types={AddressType.XCH}. NFT/DID/other prefixed addresses that previously may have passed the simple prefix check will now be rejected. Confirm this stricter validation is intentional and doesn't break existing clients sending to non-XCH-typed addresses on the same network.

issues.description: cat_spend drops MAX_COIN_AMOUNT validation on additions
issues.detail: Old cat_spend explicitly raised when addition.amount > MAX_COIN_AMOUNT. The new code forwards additions to create_signed_transaction without this check. If create_signed_transaction does not enforce the same cap, large-amount requests that previously failed fast will now proceed further before failing (or succeed unexpectedly). Verify equivalent enforcement downstream.

issues.description: Memos forwarding semantics changed for cat_spend with additions
issues.detail: Original code per-addition encoded memos only when addition.memos was not None and built a memos list aligned to amounts. New code passes request.additions through verbatim to CreateSignedTransaction. If create_signed_transaction handles per-Addition memos differently (e.g., encoding, None handling, alignment with prepended primary output), memo ordering/encoding for CAT spends could regress silently.

issues.description: Test changes mask the previous empty-additions code path
issues.detail: Tests replaced additions=[] with additions=[Addition(amount=0, puzzle_hash=zeros)]. The prior path tested CATSpend with empty additions falling back to amount/inner_address. That fallback branch still exists in the new code but is no longer exercised in this test. Add a dedicated test for the request.additions is None fallback to avoid coverage regression.

issues.description: send_transaction no longer wraps memos as outer list; relies on Addition.memos type
issues.detail: Old code passed memos=[[mem.encode... for mem in request.memos]] (list of list of bytes). New code constructs Addition(..., request.memos) where Addition.memos is list[str] | None. The conversion to per-addition byte memos must happen inside create_signed_transaction; confirm it produces identical wire format. A mismatch could change memo semantics on chain.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy_validation duplicates logic across two request types via free function
issues.detail: Pulling the validator out into a free function then re-exposing it as a property on both CATSpend and CreateSignedTransaction works but spreads the contract. Consider a shared mixin or keeping a single canonical owner so future schema changes (e.g., extra_delta type) update in one place and stay testable.

review.summary: The refactor consolidates send_transaction and cat_spend onto create_signed_transaction, which is a sensible simplification, but several behavioral details deserve verification: address validation tightens from prefix-only to AddressType.XCH, the explicit MAX_COIN_AMOUNT check on CAT additions is removed, and memo construction is delegated to the downstream endpoint with a different shape. Tests were updated in a way that no longer exercises the empty-additions fallback. The shared cat_discrepancy_validation helper is fine but mildly duplicates surface area across two request types.
